2006.11239: Established the standard forward-noising and reverse-denoising training framework that underlies the diffusion objective used by DiT.
2010.02502: Introduced a non-Markovian implicit process that reuses the same training objective while reducing sampling steps, laying the groundwork for deterministic and few-step DiT inference.
2011.13456: Unified score models and diffusion through continuous-time SDEs and probability-flow ODEs, providing the theoretical basis for flow, ODE, and solver-based views.
2112.10752: Moved diffusion from pixel space into an autoencoder latent and introduced cross-attention conditioning, directly shaping the representation and conditioning interface of latent DiT models.
2202.00512: Progressively distilled multi-step samplers into fewer steps, an early template for modern few-step DiT and video-generation distillation.
2204.03458: Systematized factorized spatiotemporal modeling and conditional generation for video diffusion, providing important task and modeling context for later video DiTs.
2206.00364: Reworked preconditioning, noise distributions, loss weighting, and sampler design into a strong diffusion baseline that remains influential in DiT training and sampling.
2206.00927: Used the semilinear structure of diffusion ODEs to build higher-order solvers, reducing high-quality sampling to roughly ten steps and transferring naturally to DiT.
2207.12598: Combined conditional and unconditional predictions to strengthen prompt adherence, and remains a standard inference mechanism for image and video DiTs.
2209.03003: Learned straighter probability-transport paths to simplify ODE integration, helping move modern DiTs from DDPM objectives toward rectified flow.
2210.02747: Trained continuous normalizing flows by regressing vector fields along conditional probability paths, becoming a core formulation for flow-based DiTs.
2212.09748: Replaced the U-Net with a Transformer operating on latent patches and established the scaling baseline for subsequent visual DiT research.
2302.12192: Applied human feedback to text-to-image alignment and established an early loop connecting reward models, preference data, and generator fine-tuning.
2303.06555: Used a single diffusion Transformer to model multiple modalities and their joint distributions, linking early DiT work to later omni-generation models.
2304.05977: Built a text-image preference reward model and introduced ReFL, highlighting reward quality as a central constraint in reinforcement learning for visual generation.
2305.16381: Treated text-to-image diffusion as a KL-regularized policy and used online policy gradients to maximize feedback rewards.
2311.12908: Reformulated DPO for diffusion likelihoods and ELBOs, providing a standard baseline for later preference optimization of DiT models.
2311.13231: Optimized the denoising policy directly from paired preferences without training an explicit reward model, reducing the cost of reward modeling for visual alignment.
2407.02398: Added velocity-consistency constraints to flow matching, connecting straight transport paths with few-step generation and transferring naturally to flow-based DiTs.
2407.11633: An early large-scale sparse-expert DiT baseline that studies how to increase model capacity while keeping active computation bounded.
2410.02098: Used expert-choice routing to improve load balance and training stability, making it an important reference for recent mixture-of-experts DiTs.
2410.07303: Showed that straight rectified-flow trajectories do not automatically yield better generation and re-examined denoising directions and training objectives.
2503.20314: An open large-scale video-generation baseline covering architecture, data, training, and multi-task capabilities.
2505.05470: Introduced online GRPO to flow matching and established a reusable template for reinforcement learning in visual generation.
2505.07818: Systematically explored GRPO for visual generation while exposing the cost of rollouts, likelihood estimation, and reward design.
2505.15809: Unified multimodal understanding and generation with a discrete diffusion Transformer, an adjacent but technically distinct route from continuous visual DiTs.
2506.08009: Trained the model on its own generated history to directly address the teacher-forcing distribution shift in autoregressive video generation.
2506.18871: A representative omni model that unifies multi-condition image generation and editing, providing direct context for the latest generation of unified models.
2508.02324: A large-scale image generation and editing model with particular strength in complex text rendering and bilingual semantic alignment.
2509.20427: Unified image generation and editing while bringing multi-image references, knowledge, and high-resolution output into one model.
2510.09094: Converted existing dense DiTs into mixture-of-experts models to reduce active computation, a lively research direction whose deployment evidence remains limited.
2510.11690: Replaced the conventional VAE with a pretrained visual representation encoder and exposed new design issues in noise scaling, width, and convergence for high-dimensional semantic latents.
2511.20645: Revisited diffusion directly in pixel space and explored a scalable path that avoids conventional VAE latents.
2511.22699: Used a single-stream DiT to unify conditioning and visual tokens, with an emphasis on few-step generation and deployment efficiency.
2601.16208: Studied how RAE latents scale with model size, data, and resolution, showing that the tokenizer has become an independent scaling axis.
2607.24665: Redesigned DiT expert structure and routing to increase capacity under a limited active-parameter budget, but still needs validation in real deployments and across tasks.
2607.28611: Explored hybrid visual modules and data-model compute-optimal scaling, moving DiT design toward a more systematic scaling-law regime.
2508.08248: Generated indefinitely long audio-driven avatars with cross-segment state and consistency mechanisms, addressing identity and boundary continuity in long video.
2508.21058: Mixed context from different temporal scales so long-video generation does not need to place the entire history into full attention.
2509.24695: Reduced the quadratic token cost of video DiTs with block linear attention and a highly compressed video representation.
2603.04379: Pushed long-video generation toward real-time streaming, jointly optimizing throughput, persistent state, and long-horizon stability rather than clip quality alone.
2606.25473: Unified teacher-forcing and self-forcing in a causal distillation recipe for both streaming video and interactive world models.
2607.06173: Compressed video diffusion for mobile deployment by jointly handling quantization, distillation, operator constraints, and quality recovery.
2607.21553: Combined linear attention with attention residuals to overcome the quality ceiling of purely linear attention in video generation.
2508.06001: Formulated dynamic training-load assignment as an online optimization problem to reduce bubbles caused by uneven work across layers and devices.
2509.11628: Expanded cache reuse by speculating when features remain valid while controlling the error accumulated across timesteps.
2509.13789: Selected reusable video-DiT features at block granularity, avoiding both coarse whole-layer caching and expensive token-level decisions.
2509.23681: Jointly optimized model quantization and attention sparsity, illustrating the growing need for coordinated system design in video deployment.
2509.25401: Unified several sparsity patterns in an efficient attention engine, showing that algorithmic sparsity and GPU kernels must be designed together.
2511.12056: Improved multi-GPU video-generation utilization by decoupling task pipelines from model partitioning and scheduling work across denoising stages.
2601.20273: Designed scalable sequence parallelism for long-sequence DiT inference while balancing attention communication, operator partitioning, and load balance.
2606.13501: Jointly selected parallelization and scheduling strategies at the serving layer, targeting throughput, tail latency, and memory under concurrent requests.
2607.11136: Reduced fragmentation with offline memory traces and static tensor placement, applied minimal mitigation only around short memory peaks, and jointly selected parallelism, concurrency, and memory-control policies.
2607.23264: Pipelined sender-side remote stores with computation in the next layer, helping primarily when sequence-parallel communication is exposed during multi-GPU inference.
2607.23844: Introduced hierarchical caching across layers, timesteps, and tokens to unify previously fragmented feature-reuse strategies.
2509.16117: Used the forward process to construct online diffusion reinforcement learning, lowering implementation barriers around trajectory probabilities and exploratory training.
2603.26599: Used a 4D latent reward to improve spatial and temporal world consistency in video, extending RL objectives beyond aesthetics toward structural constraints.
2604.24764: Used computable 3D constraints as reinforcement signals to improve geometry and world consistency in text-to-video generation.
2605.15458: Trained video models with verifiable rewards for rule-following and reasoning tasks, emphasizing capability learning rather than preference alignment alone.
2606.19004: Reduced the cost of DiT reinforcement-learning rollouts through seed exploration and coordinated use of inexpensive elastic GPUs.
2606.23626: Reused representations from the generative DiT to build a reward model, narrowing the representation gap between generator and evaluator.
2607.17572: Aggregated Jacobian and group-gradient information to reduce the variance and computation of diffusion GRPO for credit assignment over long denoising trajectories.
2509.11865: Generated robot action trajectories with a DiT and transferred them across embodiments, representing the continuous-action diffusion-policy route.
2509.24579: Added a U-shaped multiscale path to an action diffusion Transformer to better combine fine local control with global planning.
2602.05513: Decoupled visual, tactile, and action pathways and used a plug-in tactile adapter for dexterous bimanual manipulation.
2606.05979: Unified future-world prediction, language reasoning, and action generation in an attempt to connect pixel-level dynamics with high-level decisions.
2606.17030: Unified embodied world modeling through language-conditioned video generation, turning future-frame prediction into an interface for robot data and planning.
2607.18367: Focused on interactive long-horizon world models, balancing real-time response, persistent state, and accumulated prediction error.
2607.23909: Jointly modeled worlds and actions in one diffusion architecture, making it a direct recent example of the intersection between agents and DiTs.
2511.21780: Used a single trimodal DiT to jointly generate synchronized audio and video, focusing on temporal alignment and joint denoising across modalities.
2512.18254: Supported interleaved multimodal sequence generation and explored a shared interface between diffusion and token sequences.
2606.16255: Unified multimodal understanding and generation with decoupled pathways that reduce task conflicts from forcing all parameters to be shared.
2606.16673: Extended DiT from images to multimodal outputs and studied noise scales and joint training across different continuous signals.
2606.30332: Unified generation and perception while explicitly preserving the pretrained generative prior to reduce capability loss during joint training.
2607.22531: Used a shared continuous representation as the prediction target, suggesting that omni models are shifting from input concatenation toward a common representation space.
2607.27011: Extended unified multimodal modeling to audio generation, intersecting with visual DiTs through continuous tokens and cross-modal alignment.
